In this problem set we will use the did_ps5.RDS dataset which is available on Canvas.  

You are working for the governor of Ohio, the year is 2025.  In the last few years, crime levels have unfortunately been unusually high.  In response to this, the governor just implemented a series of policies designed to bring crime rates back down.  The policies will roll out in early 2026, so that is the earliest they could have an impact.

**For each regression in this problem set, be sure to display coefficient estimates by running summary(model_name)$coefficients at the end of the code chunk**

Your job is to show quantitatively whether those policies were effective.  You have data from municipalities in Ohio (coded as state==1) as well as 19 other states. 


```{r,echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
packages = c("tidyverse","plm","ggplot2")

#this function checks if you have the necessary packages
#if you have them it loads them, if you don't it installs and loads them
package.check <- lapply(packages, FUN = function(x) {
  if (!require(x, character.only = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(x, dependencies = TRUE)
    library(x, character.only = TRUE)
  }
})
```

First, load the data and create the variables you will need to run the standard DiD specification:

$Y_{st} = Treat_s + Post_t + Treat_s*Post_t$


```{r}
ps_data <- readRDS("../data/ps5_did.rds")

ps_data <- ps_data |> 
  mutate(
    Treat_s = ifelse(state == 1, 1, 0),
    Post_t = ifelse(year >= 2026, 1, 0),
  )
```

Now run the specification and display the coefficient estimates

```{r,echo=TRUE}
did_specification <- lm(Y ~ Treat_s + Post_t + (Treat_s*Post_t),
                        data = ps_data)

summary(did_specification)$coefficients
```

Now, run the Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE version):

$Y_{st} = \gamma_t + \delta_s + Treat_s*Post_t$

Where $\gamma_t$ and $\delta_s$ are year and state fixed effects, respectively.

Hint: look at the regressions from PS4 for an example of how to add state and year 
fixed effects.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
twfe_specification <- plm(Y ~ Treat_s + Post_t + (Treat_s*Post_t),
                          data = ps_data,
                          index = c("state", "year"),
                          model = "within",
                          effect = "twoways")

summary(twfe_specification)$coefficients
```

Are the coefficients different?  Are they about the same? Why are they not identical?
